land.text: "the entire Irrawaddy valley between Prome in the south and Tagaung in the north", Upper Burma "from Tagaung to Tharrawaddy"

predecessors.note: Infobox predecessor Myinsaing. Cliopatria's Pinya shape of 1314 is cell for cell Myinsaing's shape of 1313 (672 cells); Thihathu, the last surviving Myinsaing brother, was crowned at Pinya on 7 February 1313.

land.text: Pinya less the Toungoo district that broke away in 1358; "He took Pinya in September 1364" (Thado Minbya of Sagaing)

successors.note: Thado Minbya, a Sagaing prince, took Pinya in September 1364 and "claimed himself king of Sagaing and Pinya" (Sagaing page); in 1365 he founded Ava (infobox successor: Kingdom of Ava, 1365-1555), so ava-kingdom is the successor of the union. The infobox and lead give Pinya's span as 1313-1365; the state is closed here in 1364 when its capital and crown pass.

capitals.name: Pinya (Kyaukse valley, near the Irrawaddy)
capitals.note: "Thihathu founded a new capital at Pinya, also in the Kyaukse valley but closer to the Irrawaddy"; the page gives no coordinates, so the point is the gazetteer's Ava (Inwa), the nearest listed place, and is approximate. Maw forces sacked the city in May 1364.

rulers.name: Thihathu
rulers.note: Founder; "declared himself king in 1309", crowned 7 February 1313.

rulers.name: Uzana I
rulers.note: Page: r. 1325-40; his southern country went to Prome and Toungoo.

rulers.name: Sithu
rulers.title: regent
rulers.note: "Sithu the regent never wielded any power; chronicles do not mention him at all."

rulers.name: Kyawswa I
rulers.note: "According to a contemporary inscription, he had already declared himself king at least since 1342", and "became the undisputed ruler in 1344".

rulers.name: Uzana II
rulers.note: Succeeded after the Maw sack; Thado Minbya of Sagaing took Pinya in September 1364.

correction.text: unchanged outline, but the state begins in February 1313, not 1314 (it is the Myinsaing outline of 1313 cell for cell); the Sagaing share of it is contested 1315-1316 and Pinya's autonomous vassal 1317-1325 (see the ledger)

keyframe_review.note: 193,597 km2 for 1314-1325 against the page's "at least 140,000 km2" at the founding (ratio 1.38, inside the factor of two): "At its founding, Pinya under Thihathu controlled much of Upper Burma from Tagaung to Tharrawaddy." The shape is the whole Myinsaing outline and is kept as the nominal claim; the page says the court's reach was "limited mainly to the Kyaukse region and its vicinity" and effective power "extended no more than 150 km from Pinya". Years: Thihathu was crowned on 7 February 1313 ("Pinya founded"), a year before Cliopatria's first shape. Sagaing: Saw Yun "successfully fought for autonomy in 1315-17, and formally seceded in 1325 after Thihathu's death".

correction.text: unchanged for 1326-1357; from 1358 the Toungoo district is removed (new keyframe kingdom-of-pinya_1358)

keyframe_review.note: 95,056 km2 against the page's "The kingdom's nominal claim became about 100,000 km2 after the Sagaing secession in 1325" (ratio 0.95). The shape and Cliopatria's Sagaing shape of 1326 share no cell (324 + 345 cells of the 672 of 1314; 4 cells fall in neither), so the split is the 1325 secession as Cliopatria drew it. Toungoo and Prome "were practically independent" (undated) but are inside the nominal claim until 1358.

correction.text: Pinya's nominal claim less the Toungoo district: "about 80,000 km2 after the Toungoo secession in 1358"

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Cliopatria keeps the 1326 outline through 1362. The page: "Gov. Theingaba of Toungoo outright revolted during the Maw Shan raid of 1358-59"; "Two Maw raids in 1358-59 and 1362-63 thoroughly devastated Pinya's countryside during which Toungoo successfully broke away." The cut is Toungoo town with an 80 km radius (62 of the shape's 324 cells, 19 percent, matching the page's fall from about 100,000 to about 80,000 km2; scaled to Cliopatria's 95,056 km2 the remainder is about 76,900 km2, ratio 0.96). The radius is my reading of the page's figure; the page names no boundary.

correction.text: the 1363 outline less the Toungoo district, ending in September 1364 when "He took Pinya in September 1364" (Thado Minbya); Cliopatria's shape runs to 1374

keyframe_review.note: Same outline as 1326 (324 cells), so the 1363 split changes nothing; the shape is kept to 1364 only. Pinya was taken in September 1364 and Ava was founded in 1365 (infobox "Kingdom of Ava 1365-1555"); Cliopatria's Ava row begins in 1375 with the same 672 cells, so 1365-1374 is a Cliopatria gap that ava-kingdom has to fill.

region.text: much of Upper Burma from Tagaung to Tharrawaddy

ledger.note: 7 February 1313: Thihathu is crowned king and founds the capital Pinya. "On 7 February 1313, Thihathu, of non-royal birth, was crowned king"; "Thihathu founded a new capital at Pinya, also in the Kyaukse valley but closer to the Irrawaddy". He had "declared himself king in 1309" and held "much of Upper Burma from Tagaung to Tharrawaddy", "at least 140,000 km2".

region.text: Saw Yun's Sagaing, the northern province of the Pinya kingdom

ledger.note: 1315: Prince Saw Yun, governor of Sagaing, breaks with his father. He "successfully fought for autonomy in 1315-17" (the Sagaing page: "In 1315, the teenage prince walked out of the Pinya Palace, never to return"). The pages give no battle.

region.text: Saw Yun's Sagaing, the northern province of the Pinya kingdom

ledger.note: 1317: Saw Yun's fight for autonomy ends in his favour ("fought for autonomy in 1315-17"); "Sagaing got a breather in 1317 when Toungoo and Taungdwin revolted" (Sagaing page).

region.text: Sagaing, autonomous from 1317 and formally independent in 1325

ledger.note: 1317: Sagaing is left autonomous under Pinya's nominal overlordship. The page has Saw Yun winning autonomy in 1315-17 and "formally" seceding in 1325, and counts Sagaing in Pinya's "nominal claim" of about 140,000 km2 until then; the status 'vassal' is my reading of those words.

1325: Sagaing formally secedes after Thihathu's death. "Sagaing formally seceded in 1325 after Thihathu's death"; "The kingdom's nominal claim became about 100,000 km2 after the Sagaing secession in 1325". Cliopatria's Pinya and Sagaing shapes divide the old outline from 1326.

region.text: Toungoo (Taungoo), the southernmost vassal: "its southernmost vassals Toungoo (Taungoo) and Prome (Pyay)"

ledger.note: 1358: Toungoo breaks away. "Gov. Theingaba of Toungoo outright revolted during the Maw Shan raid of 1358-59" and the page puts the nominal claim at "about 80,000 km2 after the Toungoo secession in 1358"; "Two Maw raids in 1358-59 and 1362-63 thoroughly devastated Pinya's countryside during which Toungoo successfully broke away". Region: Toungoo town with an 80 km radius, my reading.

region.text: Pinya, taken by Thado Minbya in September 1364

ledger.note: September 1364: Thado Minbya of Sagaing takes Pinya. "He took Pinya in September 1364", after the Maw forces had "sacked Sagaing in April 1364" and "sacked the city in May"; the Sagaing page has him "claimed himself king of Sagaing and Pinya". Pinya's land passes to the Sagaing crown.

region.text: Pinya less Toungoo, passing to the king of Sagaing and then to Ava

ledger.note: September 1364: the Pinya Kingdom ends when Thado Minbya takes the city; he founds Ava in 1365 ("founded the Ava kingdom in 1365"). The infobox and lead give the span as 1313-1365 and name Ava as successor; the 1364 date is the page's "He took Pinya in September 1364".

wars.name: Saw Yun's war of autonomy (Sagaing)

zones.text: Sagaing, the northern province governed by Saw Yun

wars.outcome: Saw Yun "successfully fought for autonomy in 1315-17" and Sagaing seceded formally in 1325 after Thihathu's death.
wars.note: My label; the page names no battle or treaty. Toungoo and Taungdwin revolted in 1317 (Sagaing page), which relieved Sagaing.

wars.name: Raids on Pinya's southern vassals (Ramanya 1330, Arakan 1333-34)
wars.outcome: "Ramanya attacked Prome in 1330; Arakan raided Thayet in 1333-34"; the page records no change of border.
wars.note: My label for two raids the page lists together; Prome and Thayet lay in the south of Pinya's nominal claim, whose southernmost vassals were "practically independent".

wars.name: Sagaing-Pinya hostilities and the 1351 truce
wars.outcome: Sagaing's 1339 expedition to Mindon, inside Pinya territory, brought Saw Yun's children back to Sagaing (Sagaing page); Kyawswa II "agreed to a truce with the northern rival in 1351".
wars.note: My label; neither page describes a battle or a moved border, so no zone is drawn. Kyawswa II then "in 1357/58 agreed to an alliance with Sagaing"; Narathu "broke the alliance" in 1359.

wars.name: Maw Shan raids on Sagaing and Pinya
wars.outcome: "Two Maw raids in 1358-59 and 1362-63 thoroughly devastated Pinya's countryside"; "The Maw forces sacked Sagaing in April 1364" and "sacked the city in May" (Pinya); no Shan land was added.
wars.note: Maw troops had "breached northern Sagaing territory in 1342" and raided it in 1356-57 (Sagaing page). In 1363 Narathu "switched sides and aided the Maw attack on Sagaing in 1363-64", with Pinya responsible for a naval blockade.

wars.name: Thado Minbya's conquest of Pinya
wars.outcome: "He took Pinya in September 1364"; Thado Minbya "claimed himself king of Sagaing and Pinya" and founded Ava in 1365.
wars.note: Follows the Maw sacks of April (Sagaing) and May (Pinya) 1364.

certainty.note: No surveyed or treaty border: "The majority of the vassal states reported in the chronicles lay within a 250 km radius from Pinya", and "Pinya's effective power extended no more than 150 km from Pinya". The Cliopatria outlines are claims, not frontiers.

sources.title: Sagaing Kingdom - Wikipedia

notes: Cliopatria's Kingdom of Pinya (1314-1374) is a 672-cell outline identical to Myinsaing's 1313 shape and to Ava's 1375 shape; from 1326 it is split into Pinya (324 cells) and Sagaing (345 cells), which do not overlap and leave 4 of the 672 cells unassigned. The row runs ten years past the state: Pinya fell in September 1364 and Ava was founded in 1365, so 1365-1374 should be drawn by ava-kingdom (its Cliopatria row starts in 1375) and the 1363 shape is kept to 1364 only. Corrections: start moved from 1314 to 7 February 1313; Sagaing's share is contested 1315-1317 and a vassal 1317-1325 (my reading of 'fought for autonomy in 1315-17' and 'formally seceded in 1325'); a new 1358 keyframe removes Toungoo (80 km radius round Toungoo town, sized to the page's fall from about 100,000 to about 80,000 km2); end set to September 1364 (the lead and infobox say 1365). Open items: the capital's coordinates are approximate (the page gives none; the gazetteer's Ava point is used); Prome and Toungoo were 'practically independent' vassals for undated periods and no event is dated for Prome; Hanthawaddy (Ramanya) appears only as the 1330 attack on Prome, with no border change; the Pinya-Sagaing hostilities of 1339-1351 have no battle on either page; the page budget (1-2 pages) was spent on Pinya Kingdom and Sagaing Kingdom, so Myinsaing, Prome and Hanthawaddy pages were not opened. Counterpart needing a dossier: Toungoo, suggested slug toungoo-principality (Toungoo from the 1358 revolt until the First Toungoo Empire row of 1502), named in the 1358 loss. The Sagaing dossier carries the 1364 gain and the 1365 handover to ava-kingdom.
